newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Czech ICEC to start paper production in Slovenia.
newsitem.headline: Czech ICEC to start paper production in Slovenia.

text.p: Czech holding ICEC plans to start paper production at Slovenia's Videm Krsko plant later this month following a favourable ruling by a Slovenian district court, ICEC's legal representative said on Monday.

Krsko district court in eastern Slovenia ordered two Slovenian firms, that had been renting production facilities at the plant, to hand over the premises to International Engineering & Contracting (ICEC).
ICEC bought Videm in March but the deal aroused opposition among some Slovenian politicians and has been the subject of numerous court hearings.
"ICEC hopes to start production in the factory later this month if there are no unexpected legal obstacles," Miro Senica, the firm's legal representative in Slovenia, told Reuters.
In March the Czech firm paid 35.5 million marks for Videm, which has been bankrupt since 1993.
ICEC's bid topped the only rival offer, jointly submitted by Slovenia's Videm Papir and Vitacel. They had been renting Videm's production facilities since its insolvency.
In September, Videm Papir and Vitacel challenged the sale in a Krsko court, arguing thet Videm Krsko should not fall into foreign hands.
The court has yet to end its deliberations but Senica said ICEC was hoping the final decision would go its way.
"They (Videm Papir and Vitacel) are clinging to a straw because we are legally registered in Slovenia and are therefore a domestic entity," Senica said.
Videm's state creditors launched their own legal action against the sale in June, arguing that the sale price was a giveaway.
They dropped their complaint a month later when ICEC agreed to pay an additional 10 million marks for a production permit. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
